description: Canonical fixed-semantics contract for v0.0.6 CUDA neural self-play throughput comparisons.

seeds.game_seed_derivation: python-random.Random(batch_seed).getrandbits(64), once per game in zero-based game-index order
seeds.decision_seed_derivation: python-random.Random(game_seed).randrange(2**64), once per ply in move order

worker_concurrency.description: Number of concurrent self-play game threads.

inference_batch_size.description: Maximum positions submitted in one shared model inference call.

queue_flush_max_wait_seconds.description: Maximum time the shared inference queue waits for a fuller batch.

output.timing_scope: End-to-end wall time from immediately before self-play dispatch until all 512 per-game artifacts and summary.json have been written; checkpoint load and one-time process setup are reported separately and excluded.

required_artifacts.games: Exactly 512 version 1 twixt-ai-match JSON artifacts at games/game-NNNNNN.json, one for every zero-based game index, containing replay-valid terminal records, complete move history, derived decision seeds, and per-decision MCTS metadata.
required_artifacts.summary: Exactly one version 1 twixt-ai-selfplay-batch summary.json reporting the resolved configuration, games=512, completed=512, failed=0, and an ordered entry matching every game artifact.

target_semantics.policy: For every recorded position, the sparse policy target is the complete legal root-move visit distribution: each probability is visits / 4 and the probabilities sum to 1.
target_semantics.value: The terminal game result from the recorded position's side-to-move perspective: win=1, draw=0, loss=-1.
target_semantics.primary_performance_target: Minimize end-to-end wall time while changing only declared optimization variables or semantics-preserving implementation details.
target_semantics.reported_rates: games_per_hour = 512 / end_to_end_wall_seconds * 3600; positions_per_second and simulations_per_second use the same wall-time denominator.

invariants.fixed_semantics: Board/rules, checkpoint/model identity, encoding, both agents, game count, every MCTS/search-quality parameter, seeds and their derivation, CUDA execution, model instance count, artifact schemas, and policy/value targets are fixed.
invariants.equivalence: A comparable run may differ only in the three allowed optimization variables and semantics-preserving implementation code; it must pass every runner validation.
